author: delegate-eval
title: ENG-11449: merge same-slug races in Postgres instead of JS
body:
## Why
ENG-11449: prod election reads froze the event loop (5.2s max delay). Pyroscope: GC +7.9s, `getDedupedRacesBySlug` +2.8s, Prisma `parseEngineResponse` +1.5s. We loaded every Race row per slug (all years, full `positionNames`, ~30 KB for LA judges) and merged in JS.

## What
- `RacesService` and the place-with-races path now ask Postgres for one head row per slug with `position_names` already merged (distinct unnested values). Same columns requested, same page-by-distinct-slug behavior.
- Merge helper in `races.util.ts`; `getDedupedRacesBySlug` stays as the reference for tests.
- API-harness test (`mergedRaces.test.ts`) compares old JS-merged output with the new output for slugs with several same-slug rows, including place trees, children and parents.

## Relationship to other PRs
- Complements merged #3173 (no overlap).
- #3153 (`fix/ENG-11445-places-race-read-share`, open) touches `places.service.ts`. Merging it with this branch gives one conflict, in the import/header block (lines ~24-38). Not stacked; whichever lands second resolves it.

## Timings
No prod-sized election DB available (restricted data stays restricted), so I could not time the three prod URLs. Measured locally against a synthetic LA County fixture (many same-slug rows, large `positionNames`), identical JSON bytes old vs new, from an earlier iteration of the SQL (I then changed `dense_rank` to `row_number`+`count` window and did not re-time):
| path | old median | new median | loop delay max old → new |
|---|---|---|---|
| places LA includeRaces | 1099 ms | 537 ms | 227 → 21 ms |
| races?placeSlug LA | 484 ms | 763 ms | 256 → 25 ms |
The races path got slower in wall time locally (extra DB work) but blocks the event loop ~10x less. Real prod effect should be confirmed in Grafana after deploy.

diff --git a/packages/gp-api/src/electionDb/races/races.util.ts b/packages/gp-api/src/electionDb/races/races.util.ts
index edc9bf8bab..7e657d259e 100644
--- a/packages/gp-api/src/electionDb/races/races.util.ts
+++ b/packages/gp-api/src/electionDb/races/races.util.ts
@@ -1,3 +1,6 @@
+import { Prisma } from '@/generated/election-prisma'
+import type { ElectionDbPrismaClient } from '@/electionDb/electionDb.service'
+
 export function getDedupedRacesBySlug<
   T extends { slug: string; positionNames: string[] },
 >(races: T[]): T[] {
@@ -18,3 +21,69 @@ export function getDedupedRacesBySlug<
   }
   return [...uniqueRaces.values()]
 }
+
+/**
+ * One row per merged race group, resolved in Postgres. `id` is the group's
+ * first row (lowest `id`), the same row `getDedupedRacesBySlug` keeps for
+ * every column except `positionNames`.
+ */
+export type MergedRaceHead = {
+  id: string
+  placeId: string | null
+  positionNames: string[]
+}
+
+/**
+ * Database-side equivalent of `getDedupedRacesBySlug`. Groups the Race rows
+ * matching `where` (a SQL condition on "Race") and returns one head per group
+ * with `positionNames` already merged, so the other rows and their positionNames
+ * arrays never cross the wire. Groups are per slug, or per (place, slug) when
+ * `perPlace` is set.
+ *
+ * The merge matches the JS one: values in first-seen order across rows ordered
+ * by id, deduped. A group of one row keeps its array untouched, since the JS
+ * version only deduped when it had a second row to merge.
+ */
+export async function findMergedRaceHeads(
+  client: Pick<ElectionDbPrismaClient, '$queryRaw'>,
+  where: Prisma.Sql,
+  perPlace: boolean,
+): Promise<MergedRaceHead[]> {
+  // Constant fragments only; every caller-supplied value stays in `where`.
+  const keys = Prisma.raw(perPlace ? 'place_id, slug' : 'slug')
+  return client.$queryRaw<MergedRaceHead[]>`
+    WITH base AS (
+      SELECT id, place_id, slug, position_names,
+             row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY ${keys} ORDER BY id) AS rn,
+             count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ${keys}) AS n
+      FROM "Race"
+      WHERE ${where}
+    ),
+    heads AS (
+      SELECT id, place_id, slug, position_names, n
+      FROM base
+      WHERE rn = 1
+    ),
+    -- Each value's first position: (row number, index in its array) packed into
+    -- one number, so a hash aggregate finds it without sorting every element.
+    firsts AS (
+      SELECT ${keys}, u.v,
+             min(base.rn::bigint * 4294967296 + u.ord) AS pos
+      FROM base, unnest(base.position_names) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(v, ord)
+      GROUP BY ${keys}, u.v
+    ),
+    merged AS (
+      SELECT ${keys}, array_agg(v ORDER BY pos) AS names
+      FROM firsts
+      GROUP BY ${keys}
+    )
+    SELECT heads.id,
+           heads.place_id AS "placeId",
+           CASE WHEN heads.n = 1 THEN heads.position_names
+                ELSE COALESCE(merged.names, ARRAY[]::text[])
+           END AS "positionNames"
+    FROM heads
+    LEFT JOIN merged USING (${keys})
+    ORDER BY heads.slug, heads.id
+  `
+}
